name: Is it better to replace my bathtub or convert it to a walk-in shower?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to replace my bathtub or convert it to a walk-in shower?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A tub-to-shower conversion may be better when accessibility, easier entry, or adult use matters more than bathing. Keeping a tub may be preferable when children use the bathroom, resale expectations favor a tub, or you want a bathing option.

Context: The change can involve more than removing the tub: drain work, waterproofing, wall finishes, glass, controls, floor slope, storage, and safety features may all change. Elite Remodeling & Design can evaluate the desired use during design development.

Key factors:
- Household mobility and bathing preferences
- Shower entry height and available clearance
- Drain location and floor conditions
- Need for seating, grab bars, niches, or handheld controls

Practical guidance: Explain who will use the bathroom and how. Request a layout or 3D design visualization before committing if the conversion changes circulation or fixture placement.

A coordinated bathroom plan helps connect accessibility goals with the room’s existing space and construction requirements.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose a shower conversion when easier entry and shower use are the priority; keep a tub when bathing or household flexibility matters more. Compare entry clearance, drain work, waterproofing, storage, seating, grab bars, and the effect on the bathroom’s overall layout before deciding.
